source_review: The driver defaults to requested=False and returns before source reads, payload construction, scope operations, or one-shot latch changes.

On request, it bounds and pins public repository source reads, compiles only the fixed default-closed R5/R27 payload builder inputs, and serializes the payload. The builder returns path strings as metadata; reviewed path handling does not check, create, clear, or reuse the R27 fresh control/claim/output namespaces.

The exact pinned Entry R2 source is compiled unregistered. ROOT_ACTUAL_ENABLED remains false; the driver sets only the fixed self-source digest needed by Entry bootstrap and calls _bootstrap_scope, never Entry.run().

The Entry bootstrap creates one production V4 scope on the calling thread. The driver then adds only the R1 helper and call adapter source rows, rereads those plus V3/V4 from the same scope, and invokes the pinned call adapter with those bytes.

The reviewed call adapter binds V3/V4 module code and state to same-scope bytes before loading/calling pinned R1. R1 reads pinned Entry R2 bytes through that scope and extracts the source-derived prefix before the unique worker-installer statement.

The pinned Entry/R1 prefix statically derives the 515 cold base plus 14 outer rows with overlap 11, yielding a 518 cold/outer union; it validates a 575-row active public map and exact 582-row active/outer union, then derives the five-row software map and support/payload union from held sources.

R1 requires 582 public rows, 5 software rows, 3 profiler modules, full union at least 582, and held rows at least 587; it performs the existing V4/R29 profiler checks after holds, then normal postverify/release and stops before the R5 installer or thread.start(). These are static source contracts, not results executed by this review.

scope_lifecycle.owner_thread: The driver records the current thread id before bootstrap and checks the opened scope is owned on that same thread.
scope_lifecycle.before_open: Strong references to Entry/V4/payload/preloaded modules are stored before _bootstrap_scope; bootstrap exceptions are conservatively reported UNKNOWN and retained because V3 __enter__ retains partial scopes.
scope_lifecycle.after_open: The scope and later helper/module/source-byte references are stored in _RETAINED_ATTEMPTS before the reviewed call.
scope_lifecycle.failure: Exceptions or non-success/uncertain receipts after open retain references, return a finite blocked receipt, and forbid retry in the same interpreter.
scope_lifecycle.close: The driver contains no release() or close() call. Pinned R1 owns normal postverify/release and failure retention; the driver adds no second cleanup path.
scope_lifecycle.receipt: Exact key set, preparation status, 582 public, 5 software, full union >=582, held >=587, 3 profiler modules, pre-installer boundary, actual CLOSED scope, and NONE/NOT_ENTERED authority fields are required.
scope_lifecycle.concurrency_caveat: The process-wide one-shot latch/list have no lock. Actual use must be a single serialized owner-thread call, as in the documented fresh interactive interpreter procedure; do not call concurrently.

path_boundary.control_paths: The builder serializes R27 path constants into payload metadata. The driver does not access those strings as filesystem paths; Entry bootstrap consumes source bindings from invoke/driver fields and ignores fresh_paths at this preparation boundary.
path_boundary.external_d_temp_targets: No D:/temp fixed profiler/R29 source target or R27 control namespace was accessed. The designated QA interpreter and its site-packages under D:/temp were used.
path_boundary.public_reads: The independent test calls _build_payload, which reads only the eight fixed pinned repository sources; the R5 payload function is a pure mapping constructor.

module_source_binding.note: Entry loads exact V4 source before opening the scope. The V4 nested V3 loader may consult sys.modules; the call adapter source-binds the actual V3/V4 module after scope bootstrap. A fresh isolated interpreter with no preloaded V3 alias is therefore required. The call adapter review separately records that it compares executable code/global/class state but does not separately compare function __dict__/__doc__ or ModuleSpec.loader; no pinned proof path was found consuming those fields.

independent_qa.observed_test_boundary: Tests cover default-closed behavior, sequential one-shot retained-state rejection, exact pinned payload construction, and receipt gate. They do not invoke requested=True on the driver, open a scope, run V4/R29, access opaque cache/software bytes, start a worker, or touch external/control paths.

root_actual_call_conditions: Treat this as preparation-only. Verify current source-index and all 35 dependency pins immediately before invocation; use only the frozen driver bytes and documented TTY procedure.

Use a fresh Root-owned Windows CPython 3.11.5 interpreter launched from the documented C:/anaconda3/python.exe with -I -S -B -X utf8 and PYTHONPATH unset. The driver checks Windows/CPython/version/clock domain but does not check sys.executable itself.

Do not preload/import the V3 alias or invoke from another module state: Entry/V4 V3 loading may consult sys.modules before the later same-scope binding check. Use the fresh interpreter and call once on its owner/main thread; no parallel caller.
Call only prepare_root_held_source_gate(requested=True). Do not call Entry.run(), R27 main, installer, supervisor, or any activation path.
A real success executes the V4/R29 held profiler proof, including reads of indexed opaque cache bytes and fixed software/source rows. This review did not perform those reads.

On any uncertain/retained result, leave the Root interpreter and references alive for owner-thread reconciliation; do not retry in that interpreter and do not add a release/close call. On success, stop at the finite closed-scope receipt.
limitations: This is sourcefake driver acceptance only. No real production scope, postverify/close, V4 verifier/R29 proof, opaque cache/software payload, or external fixed-source consumer was exercised.
The reviewed driver tests do not exercise the requested=True source-scope lifecycle or its retained references; lifecycle and no-extra-release behavior were reviewed statically.
The module binding caveat above is inherited from the separately reviewed call adapter.
No worker installer, thread/process, control/claim creation, SDK/provider/account/native/network/WinAPI action or activation occurred. No actual Root authority was exercised.

The receipt gate does not type-check public_rows, software_rows, or profiler_modules as int; exact pinned R1 currently produces them from len(), but the gate accepts numerically equal floats if supplied a fabricated receipt.
receipt_gate_caveat: The gate enforces type int for full_union_rows and held_rows, but public_rows/software_rows/profiler_modules use equality only, so float equivalents could pass a fabricated receipt. The pinned call adapter produces these values from len() as ints and is source-bound; the fake tests do not test non-integer equivalents. Consider exact int checks before relying on the receipt as a standalone contract.
